newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS FOR MARSEILLE V AUXERRE MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS FOR MARSEILLE V AUXERRE MATCH.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Marseille and Auxerre ahead of their French first division meeting on Sunday at the Velodrome stadium (1930 GMT).

Strategy: Marseille have tended to play with three at the back at home and four away. They are unlikely to alter this strategy in defence against Auxerre. But coach Gerard Gili will no doubt look again at his plan in the 3-2 League Cup victory over the same side in midweek when Hamada Jambay, normally a right back, played on the left to mark Steve Marlet but the Auxerre danger man still managed to score twice.

Strengths: The talent of their players, capable of very good performances on their day, such as Germany's goalkeeper Andreas Koepke, local boys Jambay at the back and Ludovic Asuar in midfield, France's Reynald Pedros and even Yordan Lechkov, the Bulgarian who lost favour with Gili but probably played himself into Sunday's side with his performance in the League Cup game in midweek.

Weaknesses: Scoring has been a problem for Marseille this season. They have found the net only 19 times in 21 league matches and, although now firmer at the back, only three times in the last five games which have included three 0-0 draws. Club sources say that, having failed in their bid to sign Brazilian striker Oseas from Atletico Parana, Marseille have turned their sights on Croatia's Vlaovic, currently with Valencia in Spain.

A propensity to pick up bookings and dismissals, which Gili put down to inexperience with the pace of first division football (lateness in the tackle) earlier in the season but which he now regards as referees being stricter with his team than any other. Marseille have accumulated nine red cards (young Italian defender Ivan Franceschini two) and 41 bookings this season, five in Tuesday's League Cup clash with Auxerre.

The Velodrome crowd, the most fiery in France, are a great asset when they get behind the team, but their reactions to a slump earlier in the season when they turned against some players, notably big name signings supposed to strengthen the promotion team, can be counter-productive.

Motivation: Marseille's desire to establish themselves back among the elite. They have had some of their better results against the championship favourites and will want to keep on doing them damage. They drew 0-0 at Auxerre and Paris Saint Germain and the 3-1 home win over current leaders Monaco early last month marked the start of their recovery and a six-match unbeaten run (seven including Tuesday's League Cup win).

Strengths: Their exemplary youth scheme which produces quality players, their brilliant scouting for potential in the French second division and Guy Roux's tactical nous and ability to coax disciplined performances out of his charges.

Plagued by injuries this season, Roux has nevertheless steered his side to the European Cup quarter-finals as winners of their Champions' League group despite fielding a different side in almost every match. In Algerian Moussa Saib he has one of the best and most consistent midfielders in the French league who is very effective with his capacity for keeping possession and using the ball simply but cleverly.

Having put extreme pressure on Ajax Amsterdam's stoppers by throwing three forwards at their defence in their away match for a shock 2-1 victory in the Champions' League, Roux sent out a 3-6-1 line-up at home to Glasgow Rangers when they needed one point to qualify and won again by the same score.

Weaknesses: Injuries and a loss of concentration, although this, which happened against Marseille in the midweek League Cup tie when they were hustled off their game, is less likely to happen in Sunday's league championship clash.

Motivation: To stay in touch with the first division leaders and exact revenge for Tuesday's defeat even though Roux does not appear to mind offloading one competition, the least important, of the four his side were involved in this season.
